profile.address: County Road 459, Widows Creek Station, Jackson County, Alabama, 35740
profile.reading:
Google's Jackson County, Alabama data center sits in Bridgeport, on a roughly 360-acre site immediately adjacent to the former Widows Creek coal-fired power plant, which the Tennessee Valley Authority ran for decades before decommissioning it in 2015. Google announced the project in June 2015 and broke ground in April 2018, building what was, at the time, Alabama's first large-scale data center and the company's 14th data center worldwide (8th in the U.S.). TVA leadership framed the choice explicitly as repurposing a legacy industrial site -- 'this storied location' -- for a new technology and economic-development use, and Google has operated the facility since 2019.

Google has been unusually forthcoming about this specific campus, likely because Jackson County has become one of its flagship examples of rural-Alabama data center investment. The original 2018 build carried a publicly stated $600 million price tag and was projected to create 75 to 100 highly technical full-time jobs, plus temporary construction employment. Google says it has since invested more than $2 billion in Alabama overall since building the Jackson County facility, and in June 2026 announced a further $1.5 billion investment across 2026-2027 to expand the campus -- alongside a $2 million Energy Impact Fund run with TVA and the Community Action Agency of North Alabama (CAANEAL) to fund weatherization and energy-efficiency work for area households, and continued support for a solar farm whose construction began in 2019 to supply carbon-free power intended to match the site's electricity draw.

Beyond power and capital spending, Google's own materials describe a broad slate of community commitments tied to this site: a $100,000 donation to Jackson County schools at groundbreaking, a later $550,000 gift for STEM education kits for fourth-through-eighth graders, water-stewardship work in the Paint Rock River watershed, and digital-skills training reaching well over 150,000 Alabamians and 17,000 small businesses statewide through Grow with Google programs, alongside more than $28 million in philanthropic giving in Alabama since 2009. Google cites the site's existing energy infrastructure, a skilled regional workforce, and favorable land as its reasons for choosing Jackson County -- a rationale consistent with siting near a decommissioned power plant with existing high-voltage grid interconnection.

What Google has not published for this address are current IT capacity in megawatts, total building square footage, or details of specific data-hall configurations -- figures the company treats as confidential across its data center portfolio regardless of how much community and investment detail it otherwise discloses.

reading.body:
No building-specific megawatt figure has been published for this facility. The operator's specification page locates the campus at County Road 459 in Widows Creek Station, Jackson County, Alabama, and verification occurred on September 3, 2026, but does not disclose its power allocation or capacity.

This facility is recorded as a distinct legal entity entry for Google LLC but research notes indicate it is very likely the same underlying operation as Google's broader Alabama and Tennessee data center program, which is documented elsewhere in this registry under the main Google operator record. No individual megawatt figures were located in available sourcing.

Alabama has 12 mapped data center facilities, of which only 2 have published power specifications totaling 9.5 megawatts. This campus ranks third by published megawatt capacity in the state, though its own published capacity is zero. The state's total and ranking are therefore not derived from this facility's contribution.
